findings.evidence: `cargo test --locked -p athena-core plan` failed: 'failed to write ... full.rmeta: No space left on device (os error 28)'. In both drain test runs, `git init` in /tmp failed with 'No space left on device'. Per the contract I stopped rather than free space. This blocks verification; it is not a defect of the change. Athena's earlier `cargo test --locked` passed 743 tests on this tree.

findings.summary: Unread free-text requests, including the steward's, are now always refused until someone runs `athena go`. Drain never reads them, so they stay queued.
findings.evidence: Acceptance comes only from bullets or a reading. Refused items are skipped and never read. D106's tradeoff documents this, so it is intended, but the steward may need to emit bullet lists, or the queue builds up.

findings.summary: The rung inference uses a broad word list ('add', 'test', 'code', 'flag'), so many loosely worded requests still get Implementation.
findings.evidence: WORK lists 22 common words. Acceptance without bullets is now the stronger gate.

summary: I couldn't confirm that the change works: the disk in my environment was full, so neither the new tests nor `athena plan` could run. Building athena-core for the unit tests failed with "No space left on device", and test fixtures in the drain test file failed in `git init` for the same reason. As a result, none of the seven behavior criteria were exercised, including running `athena plan` with `cargo run`. Reading the change, it looks right and in scope. The two defaults that kept the refusal gate from firing are removed: every job getting the Implementation rung, and a request's first line counting as acceptance. A deterministic planning pass now fills the plan fields from the records and the repository's tracked files, raises open questions for missing paths and unknown job ids, and refuses vague items. The new `athena plan` command prints the plan and says when nothing is open. There is a test written for each behavior criterion. The three content criteria are met, and only the 10 expected files changed. Athena's earlier checks on this tree passed: fmt, clippy, and 743 tests. The verdict is fail only because the behavior could not be checked; it should be re-verified once there is disk space. One minor point: free-text requests without a bullet list (including the steward's) now stay queued until someone runs `athena go` on them. The decision entry (D106) documents this as intended.
